ComponentTypes.name: Object Storage
ComponentTypes.description: A cloud storage mechanism used for storing data, resources, and metadata, accessible via IAM, signed URLs, or public access.

ComponentTypes.name: Virtual Private Cloud (VPC)
ComponentTypes.description: A secure, isolated private cloud hosted within a public cloud account, used to create logical network boundaries.

ComponentTypes.name: Public Subnet
ComponentTypes.description: A network subnet containing routing elements to allow housed components (like front-end apps or load balancers) to connect directly to the internet.

ComponentTypes.name: Private Subnet
ComponentTypes.description: A network subnet housing sensitive components (like databases or backends) that should not have direct internet access, receiving traffic via protected routing.

ComponentTypes.name: API Gateway
ComponentTypes.description: An internet-facing component acting as an initial touchpoint and entry interface for backend services and compute instances.

ComponentTypes.name: Load Balancer
ComponentTypes.description: An initial touchpoint component often placed in a public subnet to distribute incoming internet traffic securely.

ComponentTypes.name: Bastion Host
ComponentTypes.description: A server providing access to a private network from an external network, commonly used as a developer access point.

ComponentTypes.name: Auth/Identity Server
ComponentTypes.description: A representation of an OAuth, IAM, or directory system which manages identities, authenticates users, and verifies authorizations.

ComponentTypes.name: Ephemeral IAM Server
ComponentTypes.description: A service that grants temporary permissions or ephemeral identities to compute components to perform specific actions across trust boundaries.

ComponentTypes.name: Web Application Firewall (WAF)
ComponentTypes.description: A security component used to monitor and block common attack payloads (like XSS and SQLi) before they reach application code.

Capabilities.name: Generate Signed URLs
Capabilities.description: The ability to dynamically generate URLs that cryptographically guarantee an entity can access a specific cloud storage resource.

Capabilities.name: Assume Ephemeral Identity
Capabilities.description: The capability of a compute instance or application component to temporarily adopt an identity to securely access protected resources.

Capabilities.name: Verify Identity and Access
Capabilities.description: The ability to authenticate users and authorize callers to access application components across varying trust boundaries.

Capabilities.name: Filter Web Traffic
Capabilities.description: The ability of a WAF or API Gateway to monitor, filter, or block common malicious HTTP requests based on curated or custom rulesets.

Capabilities.name: Rate Limit APIs
Capabilities.description: The capability to throttle or restrict the volume of requests to sensitive API endpoints to prevent abuse or service overload.

Capabilities.name: Log and Monitor Activity
Capabilities.description: The ability to record Layer 7 HTTP calls, internal actor metadata, and trace IDs, and emit alerts on functional anomalies.

Threats.name: Public Storage Data Leak
Threats.description: Unauthenticated, public access to object storage leading to the accidental leak or malicious reconnaissance of sensitive files.

Threats.name: IAM Credential Compromise
Threats.description: Loss or hardcoding of persistent control plane IAM credentials, granting an attacker broad access to managed cloud systems.

Threats.name: Signed URL Generation Injection
Threats.description: Code injection vulnerability in custom or dynamic application logic used to generate cryptographically signed storage URLs.

Threats.name: Signed URL Leakage
Threats.description: Anonymous access to protected storage resources via a leaked signed URL, typically exacerbated by inadequate expiration constraints.

Threats.name: Insecure Bastion Access
Threats.description: Exploitation of a poorly engineered or improperly deployed bastion host to bypass external protections and gain unauthorized entry into a private subnet.

Threats.name: Direct Backend Exposure
Threats.description: Placing databases or unhardened backend systems in public subnets, directly exposing them to targeted internet-based attacks.

Threats.name: Untrusted Input Injection
Threats.description: Passing dangerous, unverified user input directly to critical application components in a 'High Trust' architecture setup, resulting in XSS or SQLi.

Threats.name: Sensitive Data in Logs
Threats.description: Accidental exposure of SSNs, health information, or PII due to failure to mask or filter sensitive payloads in application and Layer 7 access logs.

Threats.name: Unpatched Infrastructure Exploitation
Threats.description: Exploiting underlying vulnerabilities in self-managed IaaS or PaaS components where developers have failed to perform regular version updates or OS patching.

Threats.name: Web Scraping
Threats.description: Automated, massive data extraction from public cloud endpoints when proper WAF filtering or acceptable route monitoring is absent.

Threats.name: Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS)
Threats.description: Volumetric or application-layer attacks that overwhelm cloud application resources, taking them offline if advanced protections or WAF rate limits are not in place.
